com.launchdarkly.sdk.internal.events

Class EventSender.Result

  • java.lang.Object
    • com.launchdarkly.sdk.internal.events.EventSender.Result
  • Enclosing interface:
    EventSender

    public static final class EventSender.Result
extends java.lang.Object
    Encapsulates the results of a call to an EventSender method.

    • Constructor Summary

      Constructors 
      Constructor and Description
      Result(boolean success, boolean mustShutDown, java.util.Date timeFromServer)
      Deprecated. 
      Use success(Date), failure(), or unexpectedFailure(). The mustShutDown flag predates the delivery cooldown: it is now read through isUnexpectedFailure() and no longer shuts anything down permanently.

      • Result

        @Deprecated
public Result(boolean success,
                          boolean mustShutDown,
                          java.util.Date timeFromServer)
        Deprecated. Use success(Date), failure(), or unexpectedFailure(). The mustShutDown flag predates the delivery cooldown: it is now read through isUnexpectedFailure() and no longer shuts anything down permanently.
        Constructs an instance.
        Parameters:
        success - true if the events were delivered
        mustShutDown - true if the failure was an unexpected error (such as an HTTP 401 error, implying that the SDK key is invalid)
        timeFromServer - the parsed value of an HTTP Date header received from the remote server, if any; this is used to compensate for differences between the application's time and server time

      • success

        Returns a result representing a successful delivery.
        Parameters:

      • failure

        public static EventSender.Result failure()
        Returns a result representing an ordinary delivery failure, such as a service outage or network error. Unlike unexpectedFailure(), it does not cause event delivery to enter a cooldown window.
        Returns:
        the result

      • unexpectedFailure

        public static EventSender.Result unexpectedFailure()
        Returns a result representing a delivery failure classified as unexpected (such as an HTTP 401 error, implying that the SDK key is invalid), which makes event delivery back off.

        For the benefit of consumers that still read isMustShutDown(), this also sets that legacy flag.

        Returns:
        the result

      • isSuccess

        public boolean isSuccess()
        Returns true if the events were delivered.
        Returns:
        true if the events were delivered

      • isMustShutDown

        @Deprecated
public boolean isMustShutDown()
        Deprecated. Use isUnexpectedFailure(). An unexpected failure no longer shuts event delivery down permanently; it makes delivery back off.
        Returns true if the failure was an unexpected error (such as an HTTP 401 error, implying that the SDK key is invalid).
        Returns:
        true if the failure was unexpected

      • isUnexpectedFailure

        public boolean isUnexpectedFailure()
        Returns true if the failure was classified as unexpected (such as an HTTP 401 error, implying that the SDK key is invalid). Such a failure makes event delivery back off.

        This is true if the result was constructed with unexpectedFailure(), or if it carries the legacy shutdown flag, so results from senders written before this classification existed are interpreted correctly.

        Returns:
        true if the failure was unexpected

      • getTimeFromServer

        public java.util.Date getTimeFromServer()
        Returns the parsed value of an HTTP Date header received from the remote server, if any. This is used to compensate for differences between the application's time and server time.
        Returns:
        a date value or null
